source: USDA Food and Nutrition Administration, CACFP meal patterns for children and infants. https://www.fna.usda.gov/cacfp/nutrition-standards
note: Component requirements only. Tally deliberately does not model portion sizes, because a photograph cannot establish them and because reimbursement turns on which components were served.

components.grain: Grains, at least one whole grain-rich per day

substitutions.note: A meat or meat alternate may replace the grain at breakfast up to three times a week.
A second fruit may be served in place of the vegetable.
A second fruit may be served in place of the vegetable.

forbidden_pairs.note: Juice and milk cannot be the only two components at snack.

daily_rules.description: At least one grain served in a day must be whole grain-rich.
Juice counts as a fruit or vegetable component only once a day.

label_checks.description: Breakfast cereal must contain no more than 6 grams of sugar per dry ounce.
label_checks.note: A photograph cannot establish sugar content, so this is raised as a label check for the provider rather than decided by the agent.

label_checks.description: Yogurt must contain no more than 23 grams of sugar per 6 ounces.
label_checks.note: Raised as a label check, never decided from a photograph.

milk_by_age.3-5: Low fat or fat free, unflavoured.
milk_by_age.6-12: Low fat or fat free. Flavoured milk allowed for 6 and older.
milk_by_age.13-18: Low fat or fat free. Flavoured milk allowed.

infants.note: Infants under one year follow a separate meal pattern based on age in months. Tally records infant meals and never applies the child meal pattern to them.

daily_reimbursable_maximum.note: A child care home may claim at most two meals and one snack, or one meal and two snacks, per child per day.
